items.title: 53342_Cozy Cole oral history interview
items.q: Jelly Roll Morton asking me to make a recording date with him... we did a recording date... that is the only time my longest acquaintance with Jelly was on that recording date

ctx.x: to get into the darnedest arguments you ever heard and the guys used to sit around there and just egg him on and he would go. So anyway, Jelly said 'Where can I get a drummer?' Well the musicians around the club didn't know me by name, they just said there's a kid over there I think plays drums. So he came over and approached me, 'Do you play drums?' I says yeah. 'Who'd you ever work with?' That's when I started lying you know, because God, Jelly Roll Morton, I'd been reading about him, I looked at Jelly, I said,…

date, which was two hours and maybe two hours prior to the date getting the drums and going to the recording studio. So people come up to me today and say, Well, Cozy, you knew Jelly Roll? I said yeah, I knew him, but I didn't know Jelly that well. And so they said, oh goodness, I know you've got to be ninety years old to know Jelly Roll Morton. I said no, I said it was one of those things, when I worked with Jelly I was just a little kid, you know, and that was my experience with Jelly. Of course after the…
I've got in front of me a Xerox of the discography--

items.title: 53342_Cozy Cole oral history interview
items.q: Jelly Roll Morton came by the rehearsal and he wanted a drummer... everybody just loved Jelly Roll Morton at the time

ctx.x: Always paid up, you know. Sometimes they were a little long trying to get that bread together, but we'd always get it, and I would say that was the beginning of my professional playing then. Then by being around with musicians, around the band box, there used to be a place

named the Band Box, a rhythm club where all the musicians used to hang out. Well when I was working these house parties, see I was during that professionally every day in the week, because while I was playing the house parties I still had an every day gig, running elevators and like that, but during the day I would always go around where the musicians used to hang, which was the Band Box, the Rhythm Club and sit around and listen to them talk, listen to them rehearse, until time to go to work, and time to go to…
I heard that some guys were just turned off by his bragging. Is that true?

items.title: 53342_Cozy Cole oral history interview
items.q: The interviewer mentions Jelly Roll Morton's band at the Roseland, but the interviewee (Cozy Cole) does not respond with any personal anecdote, confirmation of meeting, or statement of working with him.

ctx.x: The people who were the sidemen must have been pretty fast learners.

Oh yes, they were, and they were accustomed to his work, his playing, and they had made records with him before, and then Jelly Roll see used to have a band in the dancing school at 125th and 7th Avenue, the Roseland. A lot of these guys were working with his band up there, so they knew his style, they knew exactly in which direction Jelly was going.
It was a working band, too.
